title: Transform to Chessboard
summary: Given an n x n binary grid, determine the minimum number of row and column swaps needed to achieve a chessboard pattern.
statement: Given an n x n binary grid, determine the minimum number of row and column swaps needed to achieve a chessboard pattern. If impossible, return -1. A chessboard pattern ensures no two adjacent cells share the same value.
constraints: board is n by n binary; one move swaps any two complete rows or any two complete columns.
Return the minimum swaps to make adjacent cells differ horizontally and vertically, or -1.
reference_solution:
def minimum_chessboard_swaps(board):
    n=len(board)
    if any(board[r][c]^board[0][c]^board[r][0]^board[0][0] for r in range(n) for c in range(n)):return -1
    row_sum=sum(board[0]);col_sum=sum(board[r][0] for r in range(n))
    if not n//2<=row_sum<=(n+1)//2 or not n//2<=col_sum<=(n+1)//2:return -1
    row_moves=sum(board[0][c]==c%2 for c in range(n));col_moves=sum(board[r][0]==r%2 for r in range(n))
    if n%2:row_moves=n-row_moves if row_moves%2 else row_moves;col_moves=n-col_moves if col_moves%2 else col_moves
    else:row_moves=min(row_moves,n-row_moves);col_moves=min(col_moves,n-col_moves)
    return (row_moves+col_moves)//2

hints: Every valid board has only one row pattern and its bitwise complement, with balanced counts; columns obey the same rule.
Check the XOR rectangle invariant, then count alternating-position mismatches in the first row and column.
Validate row/column one counts, choose the only parity for odd n or cheaper parity for even n, and halve mismatches.
Whole-row and whole-column swaps are independent once the complement structure holds, and each swap fixes two misplaced patterns.
